title: Make them the hero
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What would make an official the hero of your story?

Jose said that in his erosion-control business, which is a nationwide issue, they approach senators. We can be a conduit of information that can save people from catastrophes: flooding, inspection issues, insurance and banking problems. How do you turn the official into the hero in that situation?

You say: this is the series of events that will occur, all in line with your values and your integrity. A student said that officials are generally in a stepping-stone position, looking to make a big impact for their constituents.
What I normally do is build their political platform on a specific issue, Jose said. Sometimes we write the part of the speech that has to do with that issue.

A student said: you have to feed them all the information, because they won't inherently know the nuanced details. Jose said: the more prepared you are, the more success you will have. Don't leave it in the nebula. Build credibility with other institutions behind you.
You should read a couple of books on political lobbying to understand the landscape, Jose said, especially if you are innovating. Innovation is always ahead of regulation.

He lived this in the telecom days, he said, and it is happening now in fintech: there's no law for it, so it must be illegal. Then they create a law that stops or limits the innovation, or creates so much red tape. That is the stance in some countries in Latin America.
He said he is trying to lobby for a crowdfunding law in one country now, and that officials often don't have the capacity to know the impact of the innovation.

A student asked: how soon is too soon to involve political figures? Jose said: as soon as possible. If you are dealing with flight regulators, approach them now. And they can also lead you to money, because people with money have approached them.

You don't want to wait for your business to be vulnerable at the stroke of a pen of a politician, he said. Be diplomatic: this could be an opportunity for you to be an innovator in the space. A student added: with absolutely no exchange for your support.
He said politicians are aware of the media and read it all the time. You can write an article that will reach their desk, and send it to them: we thought you would like to read this.
Who do you need to meet before the pen moves?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the problem you solve that an official cares about.
Write how the official could be the hero of your story.
Write the information you would hand them in one page.
Write which institutions would stand behind you.
Write when you will first approach them, and what you will not offer.

check.q: What did Jose say about innovation and regulation?
choices: Innovation is always ahead of regulation

check.q: When did Jose say to approach the officials?
What did Jose say you might do with an article?
choices: Write it so it reaches their desk

recap: Help officials be the hero. Start early. Offer information, never an exchange.
